articles.title: 广汽昊铂官宣全新跨界车型：主打宽阔低趴，明年见
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，在今天（27 日）上午开幕的 2026 广州车展上，广汽昊铂宣布即将推出全新的跨界车型。该车基于概念车“大地 Earth”打造，拥有宽阔低趴、优雅舒展的姿态，将于 2027 年正式亮相。不过，截至IT之家发稿，官方尚未公布新车更详细的信息。说回前面提到的“大地 Earth”概念车，其在 2025 上海车展首秀，官方称其为一款“集前瞻设计、尖端科技与可持续理念于一身”的未来座驾。新车外观采用了“熔岩流动”设计语言，以黑曜石色为主色调，车身的姿态较低，线条借鉴风蚀地貌的天然曲线，整车风阻系数仅 0.19。这款概念车搭载广汽最新“星灵 2.0”电子电气架构，支持 L4 级自动驾驶，同时实现首创“地磁导航系统”，可通过分析地球磁场变化实现无 GPS 环境下的精准定位。官方表示，该系统使车辆在隧道、地下停车场等场景也能确保行车安全。新车搭载了昊铂自研“固态电池 2.0”技术，能量密度超 500Wh/kg，同时得益于整车的轻量化设计，CLTC 续航里程可达 1200km。同时，其车顶、引擎盖覆盖了高效柔性太阳能薄膜，日均发电量可补充 50km 续航。

articles.title: 追短剧“上头”大脑真的会变笨吗，专家称多数人充分休息后可恢复、长期损害适应社会能力
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，据《中国网络视听发展研究报告（2026）》显示，截至去年底，微短剧应用人均单日使用时长达 129 分钟。不少人感叹，追短剧太“上头”，但刷剧后，会格外空虚，记忆力和注意力都明显下滑。那么，究竟为什么人们刷短剧会停不下来？刷短剧真的会让人变笨吗？据央视新闻今日报道，专家介绍，短剧的叙事设计里藏着两层心理机制：一方面，它依靠高密度反转剧情，用间歇性、脉冲式的刺激，持续拉动多巴胺分泌，不断勾起观众的期待；另一方面，它抓住人们的情感诉求与自我实现的渴望，虚构出与现实生活截然相反的世界，用幻想提供情绪抚慰。专家称，在刷短剧的过程中，人处于多巴胺水平较高的愉悦状态，神经递质高频消耗，处理日常事务就容易疲惫，信息加工效率明显下降，会给人以“变笨”的感觉。对多数人而言，这种变化属于暂时性、可逆的认知状态波动，并非认知能力发生永久性损伤，充分休息后可以恢复，无需过度焦虑紧张。首都医科大学附属北京安定医院临床心理病区主任刘竞：无论是“数字痴呆症”还是“数码痴呆症”，在精神科疾病的诊断标准系统里面，其实没有疾病诊断。报道提到，短视频和短剧，都能够“劫持”多巴胺系统，让大脑不断发出“奖赏信号”，不用付出现实行动，就能快速获得愉悦感，二者都容易让人上瘾。但从认知模式到心理感受，沉迷短视频和沉迷短剧，存在明显区别。中国科学院计算技术研究所研究员张语轩介绍，短视频是一个碎片化的信息流，同时具有信息属性和情绪消费属性，蕴含着人们的社交信息，和人们分享自己的生活，分享消息。而短剧已经几乎没有信息属性，几乎没有任何有效信息，基本上是纯粹的情绪消费产品。中国科学院计算技术研究所研究员张语轩认为，当下流行的短剧，按情绪价值可分为爽、燃、甜、虐、哭、奇六类，对应观众不同的心理诉求。重生穿越、携记忆逆袭的剧情满足掌控欲；霸道总裁式的故事，营造被无条件偏爱的体验；隐忍受委屈、最后苦尽甘来的桥段，帮人释放压抑情绪。心理诉求越强烈的人，往往越容易沉迷短剧。然而，长期过度沉浸，可能会削弱人们应对现实、维系真实人际关系的能力。中国科学院计算技术研究所研究员张语轩：不需要任何努力，直接提供最高强度的情感满足。但回到现实中，所有的社会关系都需要努力去建设和维护。所以长期来说，它就损害我们适应社会的能力，损害我们适应现实、改造现实的能力。此外，青少年和老年人是最容易被短剧偷走注意力的群体，格外需要控制短剧观看时长。老年人脱离职场后信息渠道本就有限，若长时间刷短剧，算法会持续推送同类内容，容易困在信息茧房中，加重沉迷。专家建议老人控制刷剧总时长，每日不超过一小时，多参与阅读、烹饪、运动等需要主动专注的活动，锻炼注意力，延缓认知自然衰退。而青少年更是防范短剧沉迷的重点人群。大脑中负责决策与注意力管控的前额叶，要到 25 岁前后才逐步发育成熟，这也是青少年自控力偏弱的原因。青少年长期沉迷短剧，可能会抑制执行控制系统的发育，这种发育上的影响，一旦错过关键发育期，很难补救。报道还称，长时间刷剧时，大脑负责自控的执行系统资源已经耗竭，很难主动叫停。一味靠意志力强迫自己停下来，往往适得其反。不妨多置身于利于专注的环境，避开容易触发刷剧冲动的场景。

articles.title: 长城汽车发布行业首个全场景物理 AI 操作系统 Coffee AIOS 4
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，在今天的 2026 广州车展上，长城汽车官宣发布行业首个全场景物理 AI 操作系统 —— Coffee AIOS 4。据介绍，长城 Coffee AIOS 4 主打“一个大脑 三位一体”，含辅助驾驶、智能座舱、智慧服务三大板块。长城汽车智能化负责人姜海鹏表示，“一个大脑”指的是 Master Agent（简称“MA”），支持全域感知、深度思考、协同行动、持续进化等。智能座舱方面，Coffee AIOS 4 具备“有眼力，有交代，会办事”三大能力。“有眼力”支持识别车内发起语音识别的人、能记住车内交流过的话题、乘客使用习惯等；“有交代”支持根据车速、车况、环境变化，动态判断介入时机，智能识别需求，优化资源分配；“会办事”支持模糊指令操作执行，包括规划路径、一句话点外卖等。Coffee AIOS 4 支持驱动 29.6 英寸悬浮一体全景屏。长城汽车还推出了 Coffee AI Sound 音响系统，8.1.4.8 三维声场，支持 4080W 双独立功放，配备 31 个扬声器和 8 个专属头枕音响。辅助驾驶方面，Coffee AIOS 4 支持“懂分寸，知进退，有预见”三大能力。“懂分寸”支持复刻老司机节奏，适用于拥堵路段、行人穿行等场景；“知进退”支持窄路会车择区错车、倒车礼让；“有预见”支持防御性驾驶思路，适用于爬坡驾驶等场景，可实现盲区预判、防御控速等。姜海鹏宣布，长城汽车把 MPCI（安全关键接管平均里程）做到了 100km，未来迭代后预计将提升一个数量级，明年的目标是 1000km。智慧服务方面，长城 Coffee AIOS 4 支持车况隐患提醒、突发时刻接应、复杂环境应对、能源智能分配等能力。IT之家附长城 Coffee AIOS 4 核心能力一图知如下：

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版车型今日在 2026 广州车展上市，限时权益价 14.99 万元起。240 智臻 AI 激光版 14.99 万元670 智行 AI 激光版 14.99 万元670 智臻 AI 激光版 15.99 万元全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版带来全新极光绿配色，前灯组与前格栅造型焕新，采用大掀背车尾，配备贯穿式 LED 尾灯、半隐藏式门把手。全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版带来全新薄荷晨曦内饰配色，升级到 10.2 英寸液晶仪表屏、电动遮阳帘。全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版配备主副驾座椅迎宾、通风、加热、按摩，后排座椅也能加热按摩。储物空间方面，新车还配备 107L 前备箱，以及最大 1215L 后备箱。全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版全系标配同级唯一高阶可变自适应悬架（FSD + HRS），带来无感刹停、晕车舒缓模式。续航方面，全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版全系搭载金钟罩电池 + 宁德时代电芯，纯电版续航可达 670km，增程版纯电续航 240km，百公里电耗低至 11.4kWh。全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版车型将行业首批开放域端到端豆包大模型。IT之家获悉，2027 年华为引望星驰辅助驾驶正式开通订阅时，所有已售“AI 激光版”车辆均将免费 OTA 升级为星驰辅助驾驶解决方案。“早买早享受，早买才免费。”

articles.title: 纳德拉承认微软放缓应届生招聘，AI 时代年轻人的第一份工作更难拿
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（11 月 27 日）发布博文，报道称在《务实工程师》（The Pragmatic Engineer）播客节目中，微软首席执行官萨蒂亚 · 纳德拉（Satya Nadella）坦言，公司已放缓招聘应届毕业生及初级岗位的速度。在节目中，纳德拉表示，在 AI 重塑工作方式的过程中，企业首先要将内部人员重新安排到合适的岗位，之后才会考虑行业招聘和校园招聘。这段言论在网络上引发广泛讨论，也让“AI 时代应届生如何获得第一份工作”成为公众关注的焦点。IT之家附上相关视频如下：纳德拉引用“AI 原生公司”的概念，指出在 AI 时代，企业应该优先为员工配置 AI 使用额度，只有该员工把额度用尽、仍无法满足业务需求后，才会再增加下一名员工。他称，未来每家公司都可能呈现类似形态。不过，纳德拉也强调，现在就将其视为长期趋势还为时过早。他同时表示，微软仍然重视校园招聘，并希望早期职业人才能够进入团队、快速完成学习曲线。他今年 1 月曾在达沃斯表示，AI 会像“导师”一样帮助新员工更快熟悉代码库，使应届生的生产力提升速度超过以往。微软还与卡内基梅隆大学启动了“PRAISE”项目，由资深工程师指导早期职业工程师，并提供相关课程。但现实数据并不轻松。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，微软员工总数降至 22.3 万人，较此前减少 5000 人，这是该公司自 2016 年以来首次出现年度员工数量下降；微软首席财务官艾米 · 胡德预计，本财年员工数还将继续下降。图源：视频截图

articles.title: 长三角铁路首次：安徽淮阜、淮蚌、巢马三条高铁同日开通，和县、濉溪、固镇、蒙城、利辛 5 县结束不通高铁的历史
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，安徽巢马高铁、淮蚌高铁、淮阜高铁三条线路今日集中开通运营。至此，安徽全省高铁里程突破 3300 公里，覆盖 16 市 44 县。长三角铁路营业里程超过 1.58 万公里，高铁里程突破 8500 公里。这同时意味着，马鞍山市和县、淮北市濉溪县、蚌埠市固镇县、亳州市蒙城县与利辛县共 5 个县就此告别不通高铁的历史，首次接入长三角高铁网络。三条新线正线合计约 364.5 公里，设计时速均为 350 公里，三线共 10 座新建车站同步启用。巢马高铁西起巢湖东站，东至马鞍山东站，正线全长约 61 公里，设巢湖东、含山、郑蒲港、马鞍山南、马鞍山东 5 座车站。该线路打通了马鞍山与合肥之间的直达通道，此前两地高铁需绕行安庆、铜陵或经芜湖、南京换乘，耗时超过 1 小时；开通后马鞍山东站至合肥站最快 1 小时 7 分钟可达。线路控制性工程马鞍山长江公铁大桥采用“城市快速路 + 高速铁路 + 预留城际铁路 + 电力管廊”四位一体过江方式，创下世界最大跨度三塔斜拉桥等六项世界纪录。淮蚌高铁北起淮北北站，向南经淮北、宿州、蚌埠三市接入蚌埠南站，正线全长约 161 公里，设淮北北、淮北西、宿州西、双堆集、固镇南、蚌埠南 6 座车站，桥隧比达 89.9%。该线是国家“八纵八横”高铁网京沪辅助通道的组成部分。开通后，淮北西站至南京南站、上海虹桥站、杭州西站最快分别为 1 小时 37 分钟、3 小时 6 分钟、4 小时 3 分钟，淮北南下高铁出行绕行徐州的历史就此结束。淮阜高铁东起淮蚌高铁双堆集站，经亳州市蒙城县、利辛县、阜阳市颍泉区接入阜阳西站，正线全长约 142.5 公里，设蒙城、利辛、颍泉北、阜阳西 4 座车站。该线是安徽首条地方主导建设的时速 350 公里高铁。利辛站与蒙城站至合肥站最快分别为 1 小时 26 分钟和 1 小时 15 分钟，阜阳西站至淮北西站最快 1 小时 13 分钟可达。开通运营初期，巢马高铁、淮蚌高铁、淮阜高铁每日分别开行图定动车组列车 8 列、46 列、18 列，均为跨线动车组列车。铁路部门在三条新线实施灵活折扣、差异化的市场化票价机制。2027 年一季度列车运行图中，铁路部门将适需增加三条高铁的开行密度和通达方向。三条线路在路网中承担不同的衔接功能。淮蚌高铁在淮北北站连接郑徐高铁，在蚌埠南站连接京沪高铁与合蚌高铁；淮阜高铁在阜阳西站连接京港高铁商合段和郑阜高铁，阜阳西站由此升级为十字型高铁枢纽；巢马高铁在巢湖东站连接合杭高铁，在马鞍山东站连接宁安高铁，向西打通合肥与马鞍山的跨江直达通道，向东经宁安高铁接入南京都市圈。IT之家注：三条高铁同日建成投用，在长三角铁路建设史上尚属首次。

articles.title: 腾讯混元发布 3D 生成大模型 Hy3D 3.6：面向专业 3D 创作
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，腾讯混元今天（27 日）正式发布最新一代 3D 大模型 Hy3D 3.6。新版本面向专业 3D 创作，重点优化了高模和 PBR 材质贴图的生成能力。腾讯混元表示，通过该模型生成的几何表面整洁、结构清晰、高模刻画细腻，贴图质量也更高，可以为艺术家、建模师、技术美术和 3D 内容创作者提供高质量的 3D 资产。Hy3D 3.6 作为原生 3D 生成模型，在训练阶段直接“学习” 3D 资产中几何、纹理与材质的分布，让模型生成可以进入专业生产工作流的原生资产。语言模型适合生成具有规则硬表面的 3D 资产、参数化零件和场景布局，尺寸可以精确修改，Hy3D 3.6 则更擅长角色、生物、服装和复杂道具的生成任务，能够还原原画的剪影与细腻曲面，并生成 PBR 贴图，为后续加工提供 3D 资产。在数据层面，混元 3D 团队组织了一套“敏捷评测 — 数据引擎 — 算法实验”的数据迭代流程。评测定义数据的“理想态”，数据引擎补充高质量及弱项数据，算法实验再将数据效果反馈到评测与下一轮数据迭代，从而让优质的反馈和数据形成循环，提升模型表现。在原生几何纹理表征上，Hy3D 3.6 通过 VAE 将几何和纹理压缩为统一的稀疏潜在表示，再通过 DiT 生成与参考图相符的几何和纹理，让生成的资产在细节生动的同时，也能保留和谐的纹理贴图。在后训练阶段，通过多专家生产多样化偏好候选，结合优胜样本 SFT 与偏好数据 DPO 进行模型效果提升，让模型的产出能更加符合使用者偏好。目前，Hy3D 3.6 已经上线腾讯云 Token Hub，对外提供 API 服务。腾讯 AI 创意智能体 Miora、腾讯游戏旗下专业资产生成平台 LAP、专业影视 AI 平台 WorkRally 等也已接入，用户可在这些产品中直接使用。IT之家附使用入口：腾讯混元 3D 创作引擎（用户可免费体验 5 次 / 天）：https://3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/腾讯云 API 调用地址（新用户开通服务后可获得 100 积分免费体验额度）：https://cloud.tencent.com/product/ai3d

articles.title: 微软承认 Win11 原生应用开发存在不足，WinUI 手写组件迟到约 4 年
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，科技媒体 Windows Latest 今天（11 月 27 日）发布博文，报道称本月召开的 Ignite 2026 活动中，微软承认 Windows 11 原生界面开发框架 WinUI 仍存在不少问题，且软件开发推进缓慢，某项缺失功能甚至花了 4 年时间才实现。IT之家此前报道，微软工程师 Beth Pan 承认 WinUI 开发体验糟糕，他表示团队已收到开发者反馈，WinUI 平台“存在很多小问题”，并且“有大量漏洞”。该媒体在新博文中分享了最新案例，指出支持手写输入的 InkCanvas 画布，从开发者首次提出需求到以实验版本形式提供，前后耗时约四年。InkCanvas 是一种用于手写、绘图和笔迹标注的界面组件，可让应用支持触控笔、手写输入及相关工具栏。对笔记、设计、教育、表单签署等应用而言，该组件是重要的核心能力。报道称开发者早在 2022 年就询问 WinUI 3 何时支持 InkCanvas；微软当时表示正在研究，直到 2023 年仍称手写功能“正在推进”。直到 2026 年 8 月，微软才在实验性软件包中提供 InkCanvas 和配套的 InkToolbar。报道还指出 WinUI 的缺陷甚至一度影响了最基础的键盘操作。有开发者展示了一个仅包含“文件上传”按钮和回车键的简单应用，按理说，用户按下回车键后，应用应再次打开文件选择窗口，但界面却没有任何反应。尽管系统已检测到键盘焦点，却未能识别按键操作，用户只能再次点击窗口后，功能才恢复正常。该问题直到 2026 年 8 月的 Windows App SDK 2.4.0 更新中才得以修复。

articles.title: 深蓝汽车：2027 年华为引望星驰辅助驾驶开通订阅时，所有已售“AI 激光版”车辆免费 OTA 升级
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日现场消息，在 11 月 26 日晚的 2026 华为乾崑生态大会上，华为智能汽车解决方案 BU CEO 靳玉志正式发布了华为星驰辅助驾驶系统。深蓝汽车董事长邓承浩现场透露，全新深蓝 S07 AI 激光版和即将上市的全新深蓝 L07 AI 激光版是行业首批搭载华为星驰驾驶辅助解决方案的车型。在今日的 2026 广州车展上，邓承浩宣布，2027 年华为引望星驰辅助驾驶正式开通订阅时，所有已售“AI 激光版”车辆均将免费 OTA 升级为星驰辅助驾驶解决方案。“早买早享受，早买才免费。”据介绍，这两台车是当前市面上唯一能体验星驰魅力的车型，当前已经硬件预埋，所有新老用户，明年都将通过 OTA 免费升级为正式的星驰辅助驾驶。功能方面，华为引望星驰辅助驾驶支持高速领航驾驶辅助、全场景辅助泊车、全维防碰撞系统。据IT之家此前报道，华为引望星驰辅助驾驶将只专注于辅助驾驶领域，与面向自动驾驶的乾崑智驾技术同源（WEWA 架构）、资源共享（云端训练算力 | 高质量训练里程数据）、流程 & 质量（IPD 研发流程 | 车规质量管理体系）。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，在今天开幕的 2026 广州车展上，广汽丰田宣布，第五代丰田汉兰达将命名为汉兰达 9X，明年一季度全球首发。新车是丰田的首款增程车型及全球首款增程汉兰达，并有华为乾崑智驾和鸿蒙座舱、与宁德时代联合定制电池方案的加持。根据介绍，2027 年将是广汽丰田的产品大年，带来 2 款全新增程、2 款纯电改款、1 款混动换代车型。不过截至IT之家发稿，新车外观暂未公布。2025 年 6 月，广汽丰田宣布，全新一代汉兰达、赛那将采用增程动力，并由中国工程师主导研发。广汽丰田还将把开发决策权移交给中方，彻底推行中国首席工程师制度，面向中国市场的车型由中国工程师主导、定义、开发。作为参考，今年 2 月，丰田在美国推出了纯电汉兰达。新车是一款三排座 SUV，将在美国生产并搭载美国产的电池。▲ 纯电汉兰达，仅供参考

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，在今日开幕的 2026 广州车展上，仰望鼎曜•山河鼎韵限量版、仰望 U9 Xtreme 两款超豪华车型正式亮相。据介绍，仰望鼎曜「山河鼎韵」限量版全球共发售 399 台。外观设计上，新车前格栅采用“大鼎鼎成”理念，镶嵌 137 颗切割彩宝石，拱卫甲骨文黄金车标。车身采用棕岩白玉专属配色，漆面运用 7C5B 喷涂工艺，漆膜厚度达 240 微米，内含彩色红铝晶片。车身侧面配有 4.8 米手工贯穿式双腰线与“1 OF 399”专版印记。在展台上，仰望汽车回顾了此前仰望 U9X“地表最快量产车”在阿布扎比公共道路极速挑战上以 503.17km/h 的成绩再创全球极速新纪录，成为人类首款极速突破 500km/h 的量产车。仰望汽车感谢阿布扎比官方的支持，为了这次测试，连夜调整出 10 公里路段，移除超过 3000 个反光标识、整平路面，才有了这条优质测试道，助力仰望 U9X 跑出 503km/h 极速纪录。细节与座舱方面，仰望鼎曜「山河鼎韵」配备 10 颗 150 切面水晶 LED 大灯，采用中轴礼宾对开门设计，前门最大开启 80 度，后门最大开启 90 度。内饰遵循“中轴对称”布局，融入山海云雷纹样微雕与园林叠景门板。中央扶手区设有钻切水晶旋钮、和田羊脂白玉平安扣与升降式扶手香氛。购车权益是此次发布的关键信息。上市前支付定金的用户，可享终身免费闪充（限比亚迪闪充充电桩）及终身免费无忧保养（含材料费及工时费）。此外，还标配三电系统终身保修、整车包修 6 年或 15 万公里，以及终身免费充电桩及安装服务。智能与日常服务方面，该车提供 10 年免费 5G 车联网流量（100GB / 月）、终身免费系统 OTA 升级，以及包含泊车与城市领航在内的辅助驾驶安全兜底。用车体验上，包含 8 年免费道路救援、终身免费维保上门取送车（12 次 / 年）与 3 年免费泊车服务（12 次 / 年）。针对老用户，官方推出了增换购礼遇。仰望车主增换购可享 80000 元补贴；比亚迪、腾势、方程豹车主换购补贴为 30000 元，增购为 20000 元；其他品牌车主换购补贴 20000 元（IT之家注：上述增换购礼遇不可叠加享受，且需提供相关证明材料，具体权益以官方发布为准）。相关阅读：《比亚迪仰望鼎曜「山河鼎韵」限量版全球限量发售，定金 30 万元》《比亚迪仰望 U9X 超跑 503.17km/h 极速成绩获 FIA 国际汽联与吉尼斯世界纪录国际权威认证》《全华班团队：比亚迪仰望 U9X“地表最快量产车”研发工程师揭秘，平均年龄不足 30 岁》

articles.title: 微软 Office 平替：Collabora Online 发现内存瘦身秘诀，内存占用最高直降 55%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，科技媒体 NeoWin 昨日（11 月 26 日）发布博文，报道称伴随着 AI 的深度运用，开源社区涌现了大量微软 Office 平替项目，除了 WordCraft、GridCraft 和 DeckCraft，以及 Starling Office 之外，最新 Collabora Online 项目宣布在内存占用方面取得巨大突破。Collabora Online 是一款基于云端的在线办公套件，基于 LibreOffice 技术构建，作为 Microsoft 365 的可自托管替代方案，可以让用户在浏览器中创建、查看和多人实时编辑文字、表格、演示文稿及矢量绘图。Collabora 团队指出在原有架构中，Collabora Online 为了提升隔离性和稳定性，为每个打开的文档创建一个独立进程（称为 kit）。这样，某个文档崩溃或异常后，通常不会影响其他文档。但如果每个 kit 都完整加载一次办公套件，内存开销会非常高。因此，Collabora 使用一个父进程 forkit，先加载一次办公软件，再通过 Linux 的 fork 创建各个文档进程；这些子进程最初与父进程共享同一份只读内存。Linux 使用写时复制（Copy-on-Write，COW）来节省内存：父进程和子进程起初共用同一物理内存页，只有当某个子进程要修改该页中的数据时，内核才会为它复制一份独立页面。理想情况下，所有 kit 都能共享 forkit 中不变的基础代码、字体、配置和初始化数据，只有真正被修改的数据才需要复制。问题在于，Linux 通常以 4 KB 为单位管理内存页。即使某个文档进程只修改了共享内存页中的几个字节，操作系统也必须为该进程复制整个 4 KB 页面。Collabora 开发者梅文 · 卡尔解释称，forkit 在创建和丢弃临时数据后，会在已分配内存中留下许多细小空隙；当文档进程随后使用这些空隙时，就会触发不必要的整页复制。Collabora 的解决办法，是在创建第一个文档进程之前，先在父进程 forkit 中把这些空隙填满。这样一来，各个文档进程的新数据会被分配到全新的内存页，而原本可共享的内存页则保持完整，从而避免被“污染”后反复复制。这项操作听起来会增加内存占用，但由于这些空隙本来就存在于 forkit 已分配的内存范围内，填充操作只是改变了内存的分配方式。据 Collabora 介绍，该操作只需在服务器启动时执行一次，耗时约 11 毫秒；在测试中，即使创建了 160 个文档进程，父进程的内存占用也没有增加。Collabora 在一台配备 4 核处理器、8 GB 内存的服务器上，模拟 10 名用户同时打开并编辑文档。结果显示，空白文本文档的单份内存占用由 53.9 MB 降至 24.4 MB，降幅约为 55%；普通 Writer 文档由 73.6 MB 降至 47.8 MB，降幅约为 35%；Impress 演示文稿由 72.1 MB 降至 50.3 MB，降幅约为 30%。文档类型优化前每份内存优化后每份内存降幅空白文本文档53.9 MB24.4 MB约 55%Writer 文档73.6 MB47.8 MB约 35%Impress 演示文稿72.1 MB50.3 MB约 30%Collabora 估计，在同时服务约 1000 名用户的高负载服务器场景下，这项优化最多可节省 25 GB 内存。在内存成本持续上涨的背景下，这对需要承载大量在线文档编辑任务的企业、学校及云服务提供商而言，意味着更低的硬件成本和更强的并发承载能力。

articles.title: 比亚迪海洋网首款旗舰 MPV“海鲸”2027 年第一季度上市：车长 5270mm，轴距 3130mm
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 27 日消息，在今天开幕的 2026 广州车展上，比亚迪海洋网首款旗舰 MPV“海鲸”正式首发亮相。作为海洋网的第五大独立 IP，新车定位为家用旗舰 MPV，预计售价约 30 万元，计划于 2027 年一季度上市。尺寸方面，海鲸的长宽高分别为 5270/1996/1815mm，轴距达 3130mm。这一规格不仅跨入了大型 MPV 门槛，车长与轴距甚至略微超过了同门的腾势 D9，为车内大空间布局提供了充裕的基础。动力系统是新车的主要看点。海鲸将提供插混与纯电双动力版本，并搭载第二代刀片电池。其中，插混版 CLTC 纯电续航超 400 公里，纯电版续航超 900 公里。在智能化方面，官方确认海鲸将搭载新一代比亚迪高阶辅助驾驶技术。但截至IT之家发稿，关于该车的内饰设计、具体座椅布局以及智驾硬件规格等详细信息，官方尚未进一步披露。

articles.title: RoboScience 机器科学发布 GenSight：如何在一个模型，搞定生成和感知？
articles.content: 热潮褪去之后，世界模型的研究该转向何处？    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       今年上半年，世界模型是具身智能领域最风光的叙事。资本蜂拥而入，仿佛只要模型能把未来视频生成得足够逼真，机器人就自然能学会理解世界、规划行动。热潮来得快，走得也快。问题首先出在概念本身，李飞飞团队今年 6 月专门撰文，说世界模型已经成为 AI 领域最重要、也最被滥用的术语之一。更根本的质疑来自实际效果，智源研究院院长王仲远说得很直接：视频生成模型可以生成一群猪在天上和飞机一起飞，因为训练数据里有科幻电影，它的目标从来就不是还原真实物理世界的规律。9 月 GPT-6 Astra 发布后，大家发现，通用模型已经能覆盖具身的一部分能力，留给专门做世界模型的窗口期可能没多久了。融资市场的反馈更直接，纯讲世界模型故事的具身初创，已经很难再靠这个概念拿到钱。在这个节点上，RoboScience 机器科学发布 GenSight，看起来像是在逆势而行。GenSight 做的事，简单说就是把视频生成和 4D 稠密感知塞进同一个预训练 Video DiT。给定一张初始图像和一句指令，它能生成机器人未来的操作视频，并同步输出每一帧的深度、具身分割和二维光流；给定一段已经拍好的操作视频，同一个模型也能在单次前向推理中直接读出几何、语义和运动信息。读完论文，和 GenSight 核心成员聊过之后，雷峰网发现，这项工作不仅回应了世界模型被质疑的那几个要害，还给这个方向提供了一个值得认真对待的修正思路。论文链接：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39232项目主页：https://roboscience-ai.github.io/gensight-page/代码：https://github.com/roboscience-ai/gensight01为什么“先生成、再估计”不够用？过去，视频生成和视觉感知通常是两条流水线。世界模型负责生成 RGB 未来视频，深度估计、分割、光流则交给独立的视觉模型去处理。这条路线可以概括为 Generate-then-Estimate：先生成，再估计。问题在于，生成和感知之间没有共同的约束。生成画面里的物体位置、空间结构、运动轨迹，可能和后续估计出来的深度、分割、光流对不上。这些偏差会进一步影响机械臂对抓取位置、运动方向和潜在障碍物距离的判断，给下游运动规划带来不准确的指导。换句话说，机器人看到的未来如果只是视觉上逼真，却在几何和语义上站不住脚，那它对行动的帮助是有限的。这正是具身世界模型和纯视频生成模型的分水岭：前者不能只追求画面像，还要让画面里的空间、物体和运动关系经得起推敲。GenSight 的选择是不把生成和感知做成两个独立系统之间的串联，而是放进同一个世界模型里联合学习。论文将其拆成三个层面的统一：统一表示、统一架构、统一预测空间。第一层是统一表示：Everything-as-RGB。GenSight 没有为深度、分割、光流分别设计独立的编码器和解码器，而是把这些模态都编码成三通道图像序列，再通过同一个冻结的视频 VAE 映射到共享的时空潜在空间。模态特异性的处理被限制在表示边界，模型内部不需要为每种模态单独长出一套“器官”。第二层是统一架构：Shared Video DiT。GenSight 基于预训练的 Cosmos3-Nano 构建共享 Transformer 主干，视频流穿过所有 Transformer block；深度、分割和光流作为额外输出，通过轻量级任务调制从某个 block 开始接入。所有 Transformer 权重和输出投影保持共享，没有模态特定的输出头。论文特别提到，这些调制参数初始化为零，初始化时完全保留预训练视频模型的计算，任务特异性是在联合训练中逐步学出来的。第三层是统一空间：Unified Velocity Pred

articles.content: 聊聊榜单之外的 Motubrain 2.0，和它背后那支不太一样的团队。    作者丨齐铖湧    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       近日，行业独角兽企业生数科技正式发布 Motubrain 2.0，并宣布将于近期开源。这次发布包括一个 20B 参数的世界动作模型（WAM），以及一套名为 Motubrain-Harness 的智能体系统。过去一个月里，生数科技把 Motubrain 2.0 的预训练搬上了公开直播：25 天，600 小时，20 万步训练，19 个 Checkpoint 的真机评估，5624 次有效真机评测，超过 1 万次真机任务执行。任何人都可以实时看到训练曲线，包括它变坏的时候。直播初期，模型的真机任务成功率一度随着训练推进不升反降。团队从训练与推理的一致性开始排查，最后定位到数据层：一批数据里，夹爪的 "开" 和 "关" 被标反了。排查、修复、重启都在直播里完成，团队没有掐断信号，放弃此前权重，从第 0 步推倒重训，学费以百万为单位计算。另一次，全量数据上线却忘了调整采样权重，成功率从 62% 掉到 45%。每一个训练细节，瑕疵和突破，都可回溯。（直播回放链接：https://www.motubrain.com/motubrain2.0-live/ ）一个多月后，这个只有 20B 参数的世界动作模型，在六项代表性机器人操作 Benchmark 中拿下五项第一，在 RoboDojo 的公开评测中，得分超过了 GPT-6 Astra 和 Claude Opus 5.5。但比起榜单，更值得讲的是它是怎么被训练出来的。最近半年，物理 AI 的技术讨论发生了一个明显的变化。过去大家关注的是机器人能不能叠衣服、做咖啡、拧瓶盖，现在更关心的是，如果换一件衣服、换一个杯子，甚至换一个从未见过的任务，机器人还能不能干好。另一边，GPT-6 的表现，让大家惊讶于前沿大语言模型的空间理解能力，也引发了物理 AI 的终局探讨。当下的共识是，大语言模型越来越擅长推理和规划，但这些能力并不能直接转化为机器人操作的成功率。从模型本身走向真实场景，中间还有很长的技术链。再加上近期备受关注的 AI Self-Improvement，如何让机器人利用真实世界中的行动反馈改进自身策略，也成了一个值得研究的方向。Motubrain 2.0 的出现，源于背后的团队对这三个变化的关注。半年前，生数科技发布 Motubrain 1.0，并提出通用世界模型（GWM）框架，尝试在同一套模型架构下统一视频预测与机器人动作建模。半年后，这条技术路线在多项机器人操作评测中取得了新的进展，有了 Motubrain 2.0。在它的众多成绩里，RoboDojo 夺冠是一个缩影。随着通用大语言模型加入评测，RoboDojo 上的竞争已经不局限于具身智能公司。不同参数规模、不同技术架构的模型被放在了同一个物理智能评测体系中。在剔除Open task维度，Motubrain 2.0 在泛化、精细操作、长程执行与记忆四项核心能力上取得 49.95 的平均分，位列榜单第一。按含 Open 类任务的五项综合计分，41.28 分的成绩同样高于 GPT-6 Astra（28.97）、Claude Opus 5.5（39.40）和 Claude Fable 5.1（27.60）。在物理 AI 领域，大家已经看过太多精心剪辑的机器人 Demo，但一个模型究竟是怎么训练出来的，中间踩过哪些坑，研究人员又是如何解决这些问题的，外界很少有机会看到。这场直播提供了一个难得的观察样本。AI 科技评论通读了这份上百页的技术报告，并与 Motubrain 2.0 团队的两位核心贡献者谭恒楷、王泽远聊了聊这个模型和这次直播。这支团队基本由 00 后组成，约六成来自清华北大，而负责

articles.title: Marc Levinson on How UPS Created Modern Logistics
articles.content: UPS was founded nearly a century ago in the basement of a Seattle saloon by James E. Casey and his business partner Claude Ryan. It is now hard to imagine modern, globalized life, and the logistics required to prop it up, without the innovations Casey and his partners at UPS cooked up during the company's early decades. Marc Levinson has just written a biography of Casey and the company he founded — UPS Man: James E. Casey and the Creation of Modern Logistics — which was a lot harder to do than you might imagine, because Casey shunned the spotlight and his contributions were virtually unknown outside of UPS. In today's episode, Levinson tells us why UPS is so secretive about its history, how Casey and his partners helped figure out the last mile problem and popularized parcel delivery, and how scientific management theories influenced everything the company did. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act.
  In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties.
  We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single layer of control. Instead, they propagate across the system, interacting with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift. This leads to a multi-scale governance structure compos

articles.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31301v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. articles.content:

Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. We show that the relation is symmetric and non-reflexive, that the dependency degree is not monotone, and we give a sufficient condition under which monotonicity holds. Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on static charts, overlooking interactive charts that enable richer and more expressive data exploration. Unlike static chart-to-code generation, which emphasizes visual consistency, interactive chart-to-code evaluation targets behavioral consistency, requiring chart states to evolve correctly under sequences of user interactions, thereby rendering traditional one-step evaluation paradigms ineffective. To address this gap, we introduce ChartInt, the first benchmark specifically designed for interactive chart-to-code generation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31346v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. Abstract: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Abstract: In this technical report, we present Taxi -- a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale. Taxi scales to millions of steps efficiently. This is made possible by a combination of scalable analysis methods. Taxi relies primarily on clustering to generate a taxonomy over steps for a structured overview of the data, and provides full SQL access for engineers and automated agents to ask complex questions. Clustering and querying are best used together in a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. Taxi also includes an experimental integration of Jev-style decision models: models that map state and bounded questions directly to typed, probabilistic decisions. Abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31522v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Abstract: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. Abstract: In playtesting games, a human operator is typically required to test most gameplay elements. In this work we present Buddy, an autonomous game solving agent which can solve long time horizon objectives in an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems. Buddy will take actions, receive feedback on those actions, and pursue a goal across many turns. No written walkthrough or model training of any kind is required, and we show that this paradigm holds in a novel environment where the agent must discover solutions via exploration rather than recalling them from pretraining. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoformalization translates a natural-language statement into a formula that captures its intent, which depends on the statement's context: the background that disambiguates it. LLMs make autoformalization practical, but their probabilistic output carries no formal guarantees. We propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy: a formula sufficient for the intent is safe to enforce, and a formula necessary for it is safe to rely on. We use LLMs to generate candidate formulas and order them by logical strength in an Entailment Graph (EG), an ordering a solver decides. Each edge carries a residual and a co-residual, the two adjoints of the entailment order, all fixed by the candidate pool alone. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. Abstract: A data analysis involves a sequence of decisions, from data cleaning to model specification, each of which can affect the reported result. articles.content:

Abstract: Persistent textual memory can improve LLM agents, but repeated updates can erode task performance. We ask whether memory-store statistics warn before held-out accuracy declines. We registered mean pairwise cosine similarity ($\rho$) and 13 additional geometry, retrieval, and graph statistics on 805 snapshots from 13 memory methods across ALFWorld, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, and two ARC-AGI settings. These methods store trajectories, rules, workflows, strategies, or linked records, using selective retrieval or whole-store prompting. No such statistic reliably predicted early signs of task accuracy decline, and $\rho$ had zero median lead. articles.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product, $A$ multiplies the rank of $M(x)$ by $p$ without adding trainable parameters. Abstract: The UCI Heart Disease data are a widely used machine-learning benchmark. We show that their chest-pain variable is stored in reverse of its documentation. articles.title: FERRETS: A Scalable Symbolic Transform for Time Series Classification
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dictionary methods for time series build bags of symbolic words from subsequences, but the accurate ones scale poorly. Against other families of methods, their accuracy no longer pays for their cost. We present FERRETS, a label-free dictionary transform built on WEASEL~2. It keys windows of random length and dilation into exact eight-bit words, adds a level word of each window's mean and spread, and on multivariate data adds cross-channel words. We compare it with leading classifiers, deep networks and foundation models included, on the UCR, Multiverse and MONSTER archives. FERRETS is the fastest of the eleven methods timed on UCR under a ten-thread budget. Of the ten others, only MultiRocket-Hydra is significantly more accurate, taking 24.7 times as long. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. While existing work has largely focused on how the state is updated and organized, we investigate how the learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. Abstract: Abstract interpretation can certify properties of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), but precise analyses remain expensive. The semantics determine the structure of intermediate abstract values while deferring their numerical evaluation. articles.title: Change Partners at Every Layer: Balanced Random Regrouping for Model Merging
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33308v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one model that serves many tasks without retraining, but merging many experts this way substantially reduces accuracy. Grouping offers a middle ground: at every layer or weight matrix, the $N$ experts are divided into $K<N$ groups, the experts in a group are merged into one shared module, and a task uses the module merged from its expert's group. Natural choices are to keep the same partners across layers or to group similar experts. Surprisingly, we find that randomly changing partners at every layer outperforms both. We call this Balanced Random Regrouping (BRR): it independently partitions the experts into $K$ equal-sized random groups at each layer (BRR-layer) or weight matrix (BRR-matrix) and merges each group with an existing method. articles.content:

Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data streams, making edge computing essential for low-latency applications and 5G networks. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable adaptation through in-context examples rather than parameter updates, but evolving streams challenge context relevance and computational efficiency. This work introduces SAIL, a framework for sparse adaptation of TFMs that reuses the model's key--value cache between adaptation events. SAIL reconstructs its support set only when drifts in stream structure indicate potential context inadequacy, while the structural representation itself is updated by changes in predictive performance. SAIL combines prequential error monitoring with online, class-specific micro-clustering to detect changes in cluster mass, class separability, and feature-space coverage. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33332v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an online learning system for short-term time series forecasting that enables proactive autoscaling in large-scale distributed systems. Unlike traditional forecasting methods that focus on modeling seasonality and long-term trends, the system targets high-accuracy, low-latency predictions for immediate future intervals for dynamic resource management in internet-scale infrastructures. The system employs a two-stage architecture: a seasonality decomposition stage followed by a residual correction stage using lightweight linear models with engineered features. By retraining models on-the-fly for every prediction cycle, the online prediction system continuously adapts to changing demand patterns without requiring persistent model storage or feature drift monitoring. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33173v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Bundesrat is Germany's second legislative chamber and a constitutional veto player within its political system. The members of the Bundesrat are delegates of state governments. Tracing the political discourse in the Bundesrat is challenging as it has a limited machine-readable corpus available. To address this issue, we present a speaker-attributed corpus of 1,067 Bundesrat plenary sessions from the chamber's first session on 7 September 1949 to 10 July 2026. In this period, a total of 53,362 speeches by 2,473 individuals were delivered in the chamber, including written statements. Each speech includes a speech ID, the full German text, the speaker's name, the date and location of the session, the federal state that the speaker represents, the speaker's role (if applicable), the type of contribution, and the speaker's gender. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon Large Language Model (LLM) agents need persistent memory that surfaces the right past interaction at the right time across thousands of turns. Many systems index by invoking generative LLMs to rewrite history into summaries, facts, or knowledge graphs--a step that is (a) costly (thousands of generative calls per build), (b) non-deterministic (undermining reproducibility and giving inconsistent answers across runs), and (c) provenance-erasing (the reader sees synthesized text, not the original turn). We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. articles.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. articles.content:

Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. Abstract: Text embedding models can conflate surface-form similarity with factual identity. Given an altered near-copy with one corrupted fact and a differently worded fact-preserving rewrite, the base model prefers the altered near-copy. We test whether hard-negative contrastive supervision can reduce this surface-similarity shortcut. We construct FOF-Bench, an 83,263-triplet benchmark spanning five domains. We fine-tune FOF-80M (Focus On Facts), an 80M-parameter embedding model, with a triplet contrastive objective that ranks the rewrite above the factual alteration. On 8,327 held-out test triplets, the base model chooses the factually altered text in 99.58% of cases (0.42% factual preference rate; mean separation -0.1650). Abstract: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. Abstract: When users assume that an AI chatbot has mental states, they are more likely to develop over-reliance, emotional dependence, and in extreme cases, psychological harm or self-harm. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present open-source FUTO Keyboard layouts and predictive text dictionaries for five endangered Uralic languages: Erzya, Moksha, Komi-Zyrian, Livonian, and Skolt Sami. Existing Divvun Android keyboard layouts are converted automatically into the YAML format used by FUTO Keyboard. For predictive text, we construct weighted AOSP dictionaries using translated Finnish lemma frequencies together with morphological frequencies extracted from small target-language corpora using finite-state transducers. This combination provides a practical way to rank inflected word forms when large monolingual corpora are unavailable. The resulting resources offer reusable mobile keyboard support for endangered Uralic languages.

articles.title: AI-human hybrid conversations: Can AI Agents Improve Discourse Quality?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33459v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversations are central to how people exchange information, share experiences, and develop collective understanding. Yet, across conversational settings, discussions often suffer from uneven participation, unanswered contributions, and a narrow range of perspectives. As generative AI agents increasingly participate alongside humans, hybrid human-AI conversations present a new opportunity to address these challenges. We investigate whether AI agents can serve as catalysts for human interaction, improving conversational engagement and broadening collective discourse. We develop a framework for introducing generic and persona-conditioned AI agents into evolving discussions and evaluate it through two complementary studies. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33468v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A looped language model repeatedly applies the same block to its hidden state before predicting each token. The number of passes is its recurrent depth. Increasing this depth gives the model more computation per token with the same parameters. Can the shared block learn from the predictions it makes at greater depth? Following prior work, we retrofit pretrained OLMo-2-1B with a shared recurrent block and continue mid-training over varying recurrent depths. In the four-pass model, additional passes mainly redistribute probability among tokens that already rank highly after one pass. We use the continuations generated at greater depth to train only the shared block through a single pass, without reference answers or correctness filtering. We call this transfer preference write-back. Write-back further improves one-pass and multi-pass accuracy on most tasks. Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to misinterpret and misrepresent regional and social varieties of English other than Mainstream American English (MAE), such as African American English (AAE), yet most evaluations of these biases have relied on synthetic, stylized or decontextualized data. This paper instead evaluates LLMs on authentic, conversational AAE to more closely reflect how such models may encounter AAE when deployed as chatbots. Abstract: Language models can stand in for survey respondents, but leading approaches build their simulated people from interviews or individual records. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33510v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Detailed knowledge of a user's persona is valuable for personalizing generative AI models and agents, yet such details are difficult to obtain and change over time. We address the task of inferring persona attributes from a single day of mobile activity logs. No suitable publicly available benchmark exists for this task, so we introduce a synthetic benchmark of 1,600 persona-log pairs. We target on-device inference so that raw logs never leave the phone, which makes memory rather than speed the limiting constraint: a day of activity yields roughly 30K tokens, whose key-value cache alone exceeds the INT4 weights of a 4B-parameter model. We therefore propose a log filtering method that retains only behaviorally distinct entries. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33612v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. Abstract: Understanding how models internally represent information is a central challenge in interpretation and control. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose dense hidden representations into sparse features, and cross-layer methods capture structure spanning multiple layers. However, existing objectives do not explicitly train the sparse code at one layer to predict the sparse code at the next layer. We propose sparse-to-sparse feature learning (S2S), where sparse features at each intermediate layer are trained to predict those of the immediately following layer, with the final layer anchored by an output-distribution loss and optimization proceeding sequentially from output to input. Experiments across eight language models show stronger adjacent-layer correspondence than matched sparse-feature baselines. After decomposition, one can verify: given a sentence and a candidate proposition, does the proposition belong to that sentence? articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for biomedical question answering, but plausible incorrect answers remain a safety risk in clinical settings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can ground responses in medical literature, while confidence-based adaptive RAG retrieves only when the model appears uncertain. We evaluate this routing strategy on three biomedical QA benchmarks of increasing difficulty and compare models across a broad range of parameter scales. The results reveal a paradox: confidence is well calibrated (AUROC 0.78--0.89) on standard medical exam questions where retrieval adds little value (+2.4\% to -1.4\%), yet becomes \emph{near-random} (AUROC 0.506) on specialist-level questions where retrieval helps most (+11.2\%). Abstract: Face Verification (FV) systems have exhibited remarkable performance in verification tasks and have consequently garnered extensive adoption across various applications, from identity duplication to authentication in mobile payments. However, the surge in popularity of face verification has raised concerns about potential vulnerabilities in the face of adversarial attacks. A simpler way to get more correct images is best-of-N: draw N images from the base model and keep the one that a picker prefers. Abstract: Alongside superposition, polysemanticity is one of the primary obstacles to achieving interpretable deep neural networks. While these phenomena are typically intrinsically linked, the Quadratic Programming Enhanced Model (QPM) naturally decouples them. By representing classes with a sparse binary assignment of very few features, QPM prevents superposition by design on its final features but still exhibits polysemanticity. Abstract: Safety-critical interactions are rare in recorded driving data, leaving end-to-end driving planners with limited exposure to evasive behaviour during training. Abstract: Discrete visual tokens encode images for reconstruction and serve as training targets for autoregressive image generators. The decoder uses these codes jointly, so a sequence of individually nearest codes can reconstruct an image less faithfully than an alternative assignment. A local model of the reconstruction loss yields a closest-vector problem with a decoder-dependent target and metric. Reconstruction-only search improves PSNR across the frozen tokenizers we test. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, which can be alleviated through sparsity and low-bit quantization. We propose JetDiffusion, a video generation system built on trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA), with custom inference kernels that combine native NVFP4 computation and kernel fusion. At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8-29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares. To further accelerate video generation, we combine VSQA with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation. Although each technique can individually preserve generation quality, jointly adapting to all three remains challenging, particularly under aggressive NVFP4 quantization. Abstract: We introduce CoSMo, a compact spectral space of body motion in video, in which each motion is a single code that can be compared and edited without training, transferred to a new subject, interpolated, composed, scaled in intensity and detail, or sampled anew. Because each frequency band is the same cosine pattern in every code, codes are aligned in time, ordered from coarse to fine, and can be blended or added without matching frames. What stays constant over a clip cancels, and keeping fewer frequencies leaves less of the performer and scene. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines multiple task-specific expert models into a single model. However, merging preserves expert capabilities unevenly across tasks. This imbalance is particularly pronounced in large-scale settings, where some tasks can suffer severe capability losses even when average accuracy remains high. To address this imbalance, we introduce Recovery-aware Task Weighting (RaTW), a model merging framework that assigns larger weights to tasks whose expert capabilities are poorly retained by an initial merged model. We quantify these recovery opportunities as the fraction of a task's labeled validation samples that its expert predicts correctly but the initial merged model gets wrong, and use the resulting task weights to re-merge the experts. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. Abstract: A surgeon first finds what is wrong, then fixes only that part. We use this idea for video grounding, where video-language models often find the right moment in a long video but write its time wrong. In Temporal Weight Surgery (TWS), a general-purpose LLM reads the model's weights and activations, finds where the error arises and repairs it there, without gradients. Abstract: Class-agnostic counting requires the user to specify what to count, usually with a class name or a few annotated boxes. Abstract: In differential diagnosis (DDx), a clinician explains a diagnosis by the few findings that separate it from the alternatives. We present DDxBasis, which explains a classifier on a frozen foundation encoder as a differential diagnosis in three steps. First, a concept bottleneck reads all patch tokens at every encoder layer using gated, second-order slot attention. A concept basis then regroups the concepts into two-pole axes, each a differential between groups of diagnoses. Finally, we read a differential diagnosis from each axis through the typical presentation of its poles, the pertinent findings of the case, and counterfactual edits of borderline cases. Abstract: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Abstract: Mangroves are dynamic coastal ecosystems that contribute to carbon storage, coastal protection and biodiversity conservation, but are vulnerable to climate change. Very-high-resolution imagery such as Pl\'eiades enables detailed mangrove mapping but it is costly and have a low revisit rate. Large-scale monitoring requires free and regularly available data such as Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 but their spatial resolution poses challenges for detailed mangrove mapping. We compare four segmentation configurations based on CROMA and BigEarthNet-pretrained ResNet50 representations with different segmentation decoders. articles.title: MotifFlow: Training-Free, Self-Contained Style Transfer from Color to Motif in Rectified Flow Transformers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Expressive style transfer must reproduce a painting's palette, brushwork, and characteristic motifs while retaining the content image's structure. Attention injection is effective in U-Net-based diffusion models, but adapting it to FLUX often transfers color without capturing the style's distinctive brushwork. Our analysis across backbones links this gap to how injected features are integrated across neighboring spatial locations. We introduce MotifFlow, a training-free, self-contained framework that combines style injection with style-alignment guidance in FLUX. Injection supplies style features during generation but does not explicitly encourage the model's native attention output to align with them. Abstract: Recent dynamic Gaussian splatting methods encode temporal change, either as smooth functions of time or as constrained updates between frames. arXiv:2611.33229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We seek to learn discrete skill abstractions to facilitate long-horizon, goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning (RL) tasks. Recent approaches have shown success by quantizing actions via clustering or reconstruction. However, these objectives lead to skills that are not directly related to what the current state affords or what the goal requires. Instead, we argue that goal-directed skills should be driven by \emph{how they affect the state} of the agent. To realize this, we introduce a novel quantization method for action chunks that optimizes next-state predictions conditioned on the current state and action. Abstract: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many hard manipulation tasks come down to a spatial constraint that only a few motions satisfy, such as passing a part through a gap barely wider than itself or separating two interlocked parts. These motions depend on the exact geometry of each scene, so demonstrations and skills recorded elsewhere rarely transfer. We therefore ask: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? We introduce RoboARC, a benchmark of 90 tasks in six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo. Every task is a frozen scene with a physics-based grader and a verified reference solution that replays bit-identically. Each task comes in a Privileged regime, with the full simulator state and resets, and a Standard regime with real-sensor inputs (camera images and proprioception) and a single attempt without resets. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Abstract: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to rapidly changing motion demands while remaining stable and robust. Recent locomotion controllers are typically designed with either a dense reward that is carefully shaped to encourage steps and penalize falling, or by using a reference tracking reward which teaches the controller to follow predetermined motions. Once a behavior that maximizes the reward is discovered, the controller ceases to learn. While generally stable, reference tracking methods focus on motor control separately from motion generation. Self-play has been proven as an effective technique for superhuman performance on several multiagent games like Go, Starcraft, hide-and-seek, and capture-the-flag. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33439v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Occluded hazards challenge autonomous driving because visibility timing determines available avoidance actions. Existing scenario generators control hazard motion without jointly specifying exposure and reference-contact times. We propose OnCue, a framework that generates safety-critical encounters in real driving logs with these temporal conditions. Scene geometry provides hidden starts and timed waypoints for pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle trajectory generation. An offline response oracle labels encounters as Reactive (avoidable after exposure) or Anticipatory (avoidable only with earlier visibility) and stores safe maneuvers as training demonstrations. On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, 90.1-96.6% of valid trajectories meet both requested times within +/-0.2 s. articles.content:

Abstract: Robot agents discover reusable skills by revising programs from execution feedback and retaining experience for later tasks. This process can fail when an agent treats an unsuccessful program as evidence that the task is physically impossible, ending exploration with revision budget remaining. We study this failure in Qwen3.8-27B and examine two decisions that shape skill discovery: I) how execution failures are diagnosed, and II) which lessons enter the shared skill library. Failure diagnosis requires the agent to reconstruct physical action effects from multimodal traces, while independent reproduction of a proposed repair does not require adequate task performance from its source program. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33586v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon diffusion-based planning for kinodynamically constrained systems requires both scalability and feasibility, yet existing diffusion planners typically sacrifice one for the other. We present DFLAT, a diffusion-based planning algorithm that operates directly on a differentially flat trajectory representation. Instead of diffusing over time-discretized controls, DFLAT denoises a compact set of Hermite curve parameters in the flat-output space, consisting of intermediate waypoints together with the endpoint tangents of each segment. Every denoised sample maps to a dynamically consistent trajectory, so feasibility holds by construction rather than being restored afterward. Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted for end-to-end driving planning, yet their performance is typically evaluated based on a single greedily decoded trajectory. articles.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
articles.content: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint. Its H-Concat layout aligns source and target frames in time, so the model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming few-step generator for on-the-fly camera control. Both models are trained on paired videos with pixel-aligned anchor renderings from multi-camera videos and static-scene captures. Experiments on diverse datasets and trajectories show that AnyCam performs favorably against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods in camera control and visual quality.

articles.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
articles.content: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos. Starting from its own estimate, the agent autonomously chooses what to inspect and uses the resulting evidence to verify point identity and refine its predictions. With GPT-6 Astra, it surpasses expert vision models in both point localization and visibility prediction, without correspondence-specific fine-tuning. We further use AgenTAP to re-identify physical points after disappearance and reconnect fragmented tracks, constructing EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories in long real-world egocentric videos. On sampled reappearing points, its predictions approach human agreement, and adding EgoTAP-4D to D4RT training improves average 3D tracking performance.

articles.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
articles.content: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

articles.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
articles.content: Image editing models can follow a wide range of instructions, but video editing models still lag behind, limited in part by the difficulty of collecting paired source and edited videos. Is it possible to transfer advanced image editing capabilities to video editors without new paired videos? We introduce Image-to-Video Transfer (I2VT), which improves pretrained video editors and expands them to new editing tasks using an image editor. It enables efficient post-training with no architectural changes and no new videos, using only individual images. Our key idea is to let the video editor role-play as an image editor: it edits an image as a one-frame video, with the image editor guiding the video editor's predictions at each denoising step. Although the video editor sees only single images during training, at test time it applies the improved and expanded capabilities to whole video clips while preserving temporal consistency. To push the boundaries of video editing, we introduce OpenVE++, an extension of OpenVE-Bench that adds four new editing tasks useful for video production, including action changes, expression changes, body movements, and scene relighting. Our experiments across three different video editors show that I2VT improves existing editing capabilities and expands them to new tasks, and our models achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on both OpenVE-Bench and OpenVE++.

articles.title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
articles.content: We present LuxAvatar, a feed-forward framework for real-time head avatar animation and relighting from a single portrait. To achieve both 3D controllability and complex facial light transport, we factorize avatar synthesis into an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy and a causal autoregressive neural shader. This proxy disentangles canonical geometry and reflectance attributes, rapidly rasterizing deformed Gaussians into view- and motion-consistent PBR buffers. Conditioned on these buffers, our neural shader formulates forward rendering as a conditional video diffusion process, bypassing explicit PBR computation to synthesize realistic shading effects under target illumination. We achieve real-time streaming through heterogeneous distillation from a pretrained multi-step bidirectional relighting teacher to a two-step causal autoregressive neural shader, inheriting broad synthetic lighting priors while minimizing conditioning and decoding latency. To further specialize these priors to human heads, we construct a hybrid relighting dataset for domain-specific fine-tuning, capturing authentic facial dynamics and physically grounded light transport. Extensive experiments show that our framework enables 3D-controllable, real-time portrait animation and relighting, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity, motion control, and lighting accuracy.

articles.title: A Mesh for Every Moment
articles.content: We present MEMO (a Mesh for Every MOment), a method that reconstructs the geometry of complete dynamic scenes, captured by multiple synchronized cameras, and extracts a mesh at every frame. Existing dynamic Gaussian splatting methods either model appearance alone or target isolated objects segmented by foreground masks, and all of them recover meshes by TSDF fusion or Poisson reconstruction, whose fixed grids limit the detail they can capture. At the core of MEMO is a per-Gaussian motion model inspired by Gaussian processes, which represents each Gaussian's position and rotation over time as a combination of temporal Gaussian kernels. The model keeps every Gaussian a valid surface element throughout the sequence and carries an implicit representation of the dynamic geometry, so a mesh can be derived at any time from a field defined by the Gaussians. Although common in real captures, large and fast motion poses a challenge that dynamic Gaussian splatting methods usually overlook. To account for it, we design a track-based initialization scheme that fits each Gaussian's initial trajectory to point tracks in closed form. We evaluate MEMO on Blender-Moments, a new benchmark of nine animated scenes with ground-truth meshes at every frame, and on two real-world datasets. MEMO reconstructs the most accurate geometry among state-of-the-art methods, and remains competitive in novel-view synthesis and training time. Project page: https://memo-4d.github.io

articles.title: Tokenisation is not in APX
articles.content: In this paper, we prove that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, meaning that tokenisation is not in the APX complexity class. We prove this for direct and bottom-up tokenisation, under both a compression or unigram log-likelihood objectives, and for binary or larger alphabets. We further show that, even over unary alphabets, direct tokenisation is APX-hard, and thus admits no polynomial-time approximation scheme.

articles.title: DexLink: Synthesizing Dexterous Behaviors from Chained Hand-object Poses
articles.content: Synthesizing diverse dexterous manipulation policies is challenging: existing simulation-based approaches rely on human demonstrations which are difficult to scale, or use generic reward functions, which provide limited control over the hand-object interactions. We propose DexLink, which addresses these limitations by synthesizing diverse dexterous behaviors from sparse, reusable hand-object interaction templates. Given key task waypoints, DexLink retargets static interaction templates to target objects using an optimization that preserves spatial hand-object relationships. It then links the retargeted poses into an approximate reference trajectory and uses residual reinforcement learning to refine this reference into a closed-loop policy in simulation. Experiments spanning single-hand, bimanual, articulated, and dynamic tasks demonstrate that DexLink provides fine-grained control over task timing, grasp types, and high-level execution. The modular interaction templates transfer reliably across object scales, instances, and categories; without object-specific human demonstrations, the framework also matches the performance of dense reference-tracking methods. Finally, zero-shot deployment of policies trained purely in simulation shows promise for the simulation-based framework.

articles.title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
articles.content: Language models think in words; then multimodal models might think in images. We test whether a generated helper improves the answer to a visual question. A model describes the helper it needs and then answers using the original and generated images together. Across 13 vision-language model and generator pairs, generation lowers mean accuracy by 3.7 percentage points, with declines on nine of ten tasks. Two unified models, BAGEL and Janus-Pro-7B, each lose accuracy on eight tasks. On VSTAR, adding a generated image to the same planning hint lowers accuracy by 10.47 points. Repeated image edits yield different outcomes across tasks. ChartQAPro and MathVista stay below their no-generation baselines, while ERQA gains three points after ten edits.

articles.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
articles.content: AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results show attacks transferring to the held-out GPT-5.4 target monitor. Our results suggest that monitor evasion evaluations can easily mislead: an evaluation using only basic attack methods may give false confidence that a monitor is strong.   The sensitivity to attack-policy choice raises a problem: interpreting any particular result as evidence about deployment performance requires justification. The transcripts produced by attack policies are proxies for the dangerous behaviour a monitor must flag in deployment. These proxies can introduce visible artefacts, such as reasoning about a ``side task'' absent from the instructions shown to the monitor, that affect monitor judgements. Given the sensitivity above, the choice of proxy can change an evaluation's conclusion. Reading these results as evidence about deployment therefore requires a separate legitimacy argument for why the proxies are informative, including any justification of conservativeness. Making convincing arguments remains an open problem.

articles.title: MERLoc: Robust Robot Localization in Dynamic Environments with Pose-Based Retrieval over 3D Gaussian Splatting References
articles.content: Robots operating in previously mapped spaces must localize accurately despite moving people and rearranged objects. Most localization pipelines match the query against a sparse set of captured reference images retrieved by appearance, which is brittle under scene change and repeating structures. We present MERLoc, which turns a single metric 3D Gaussian Splatting scan into a dense Functional Reference Memory. Reference views are sampled over the navigable space for the robot's morphology and sensors at a target density and rendered offline. Pre-encoding them for the chosen off-the-shelf localizer removes the reference encoder from inference. A pose-based retrieval strategy then selects references by spatial proximity and viewing direction rather than appearance, sidestepping visual ambiguities whenever a prior exists. Across one classical and four learned localizers in simulated and real dynamic scenes, pose-based retrieval matches or outperforms appearance retrieval in most cases, even when the latter is gated by the same prior. On real data, it lowers position RMSE by 15-60 % in nine of ten backend/split combinations, and the rendered memory outperforms real-image caches posed by Structure-from-Motion. The system runs onboard a Jetson Orin NX at 5 Hz, enabling a navigation policy to successfully traverse a hallway with people roaming and rearranging objects.

articles.title: DynMF2: Rigid Motion Factorization by Expectation-Maximization for Monocular 4D Reconstruction and Motion Segmentation
articles.content: A single casual video leaves a moving scene under-determined: a point seen once from each place can slide toward or away from the camera and still match every frame. We constrain the reconstruction with the structure of the motion itself. Building on DynMF, we model a scene's motion as a handful of SE(3) trajectories, each rigid, and let every point follow one of them alone, never a blend. DynMF2 computes this factorization directly from 3D point trajectories, with no rendering, by Expectation-Maximization (EM). Its M-step fits, in closed form, every rigid motion to the points assigned to it, and its E-step reassigns every point to the motion that explains it with the least error. The background is simply one more motion, the camera's, so no masks are needed. Three tools then revise the factorization: requery adds trajectories where the rendering shows parts the tracker missed, merge joins motions that move together, and split separates those that do not. Thus the number of motions follows the scene. Without masks, DynMF2 clearly outperforms the mask-based baselines in view synthesis on iPhone and NVIDIA and in 3D tracking on iPhone. It recovers what masks leave out, from thin parts and details to small movers far in the background. Its motions segment the moving parts of MOVi-F and iTACO scenes competitively, although DynMF2 is never trained to segment. What moves in a scene is not decided in advance: it emerges from the rigid motions themselves.

articles.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
articles.content: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.

articles.title: High-Fidelity Image Matting with Pixel-Space Diffusion Transformers
articles.content: Diffusion models have shown strong potential for image matting by transferring generative priors learned from large-scale pretraining. However, existing approaches largely rely on latent diffusion models, whose compressed representations and VAE-based reconstruction introduce a mismatch with the high-frequency precision required for matting. We present PixelMatte, a framework that adapts pretrained pixel-space diffusion transformers for high-fidelity image matting. We show that strong image-conditioned matting capabilities can be acquired even from a pure text-to-image model without paired image-to-image pretraining. Our approach reuses the backbone's native patch embedding to jointly process the input image, trimap, and noisy alpha matte as spatially aligned tokens, enabling direct pixel-space prediction without additional condition encoders or adapters. With pixel-accurate synthetic supervision and real-image fine-tuning, PixelMatte predicts alpha mattes in a single forward pass. Two lightweight calibration modules, LayerShift and High-Pass Refiner, further improve regional opacity accuracy and boundary fidelity. Experiments across four benchmarks and two distinct pixel diffusion backbones demonstrate substantial improvements over existing methods, reducing SAD and gradient errors by 24-44% relative to RenderMatte on P3M-500-NP and AM-2K, while achieving competitive performance on AIM-500 and RenderMatte-2K. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pixel-space generative priors for precision-sensitive image matting. Project page: https://white-yc.github.io/pixelmatte/.

articles.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
articles.content: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of generated traces. Its estimated generation cost per recovered problem is nearly identical, while its cost per accepted trace is 30% lower. Post-training Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on traces mined by DART achieves the highest point estimate in five of six evaluations across MATH-500 and AIME benchmarks. These results demonstrate that revisiting rejected traces with DART can expand problem coverage and provide effective post-training data.
